sources.entry: AutoDoc - Private, local-first meeting notes with on-device transcription and AI summaries.

summary.one_liner: AutoDoc is an open-source, local-first meeting notes app for macOS and Windows that records screen and meeting audio, transcribes on-device, and generates editable notes with clickable timestamps for replay.
summary.what_it_does: It records screen, microphone, and system audio as separate streams, labeling the microphone as "Me" and combined system audio as "Them" without identifying individual remote participants. Transcription runs on-device (MLX Whisper on Apple Silicon Macs, Parakeet or Whisper on Windows), and notes are generated through a local Ollama instance that AutoDoc manages. Users can edit summaries and topics, copy them as plain text, or export to PDF, Word, or Markdown. The app offers full-text search across transcripts and notes, an Ask AI feature over past meetings that runs on-device, and calendar integration with Google and Microsoft for per-event auto-record. Meeting detection for Zoom, Meet, Teams, Webex, and Slack offers to start recording. Recordings, transcripts, notes, and metadata are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM.
use_cases: generate meeting notes and summaries locally
ask questions over meeting history offline
export meeting notes to PDF, Word, or Markdown
how_to_run: Download the macOS .dmg or Windows .exe installer from the latest release
Open the installer and move AutoDoc to Applications (macOS) or run the setup prompts (Windows)
Launch AutoDoc and grant Screen Recording, Microphone, and system audio permissions on first run
Allow the one-time model download (~10 GB)
To build from source: git clone the repo, cd AutoDoc, npm ci
Run npm run build:mac or npm run build:win, or npm run dev for development
notable: Fully local pipeline: transcription, notes, and Ask AI run on-device with no AutoDoc account or API key
Click a note's timestamp to jump to that moment in the screen recording
Multi-track capture keeps microphone and system audio as separate streams
AES-256-GCM encryption at rest, with the key protected by macOS Keychain or Windows DPAPI when available
Supports 27 meeting languages on supported hardware, with lower-spec profiles for 8 GB machines
caveats: Requires Apple Silicon on Mac (no Intel or Rosetta fallback) and does not support Windows on ARM; Windows needs x64 with 8 GB RAM minimum
Needs about 10 GB of free storage for first-run model downloads and internet access for that first download
Action items are currently omitted from generated notes while Next Steps is disabled, and generated notes should be reviewed before relying on them
